gloss: sense of fulfillment; worth doing; rewarding

definitions.gloss: sense of fulfillment; being worth doing; rewarding quality
definitions.explanation: The feeling that an activity is meaningful and worth the effort. Something that makes one feel satisfied and motivated when doing or accomplishing it.

examples.japanese: この{仕事|しごと}はやり{甲斐|がい}がある。
やり{甲斐|がい}を{感|かん}じられる{仕事|しごと}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: I'm looking for a job where I can feel a sense of fulfillment.

examples.japanese: {難|むずか}しい{課題|かだい}だからこそ、やり{甲斐|がい}がある。
examples.english: Precisely because it's a difficult challenge, it's worth doing.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・やり{甲斐|がい}がある (to be rewarding/worth doing)
・やり{甲斐|がい}を{感|かん}じる (to feel a sense of fulfillment)
・やり{甲斐|がい}のある{仕事|しごと} (a rewarding job)

PRODUCTIVE PATTERN 〜{甲斐|がい}:
The suffix 〜{甲斐|がい} attaches to verb stems to mean "worth doing [verb]":
・{生|い}き{甲斐|がい} (reason for living, purpose in life)
・{読|よ}み{甲斐|がい} (worth reading)
・{見|み}{甲斐|がい} (worth seeing)
・{食|た}べ{甲斐|がい} (worth eating)

WORK CULTURE:
やり{甲斐|がい} is commonly discussed in Japanese workplace contexts, where finding meaning in one's work is highly valued. Job satisfaction surveys often include やり{甲斐|がい} as a key metric.

WRITING NOTE:
Often written in hiragana as やりがい in casual contexts.
